saw_lines: Prize game buyers decide on the one prize they can picture winning, then judge whether a win is actually guaranteed.
So the sale is won or lost in the first line, where the prize and the guarantee must be stated plainly before the buyer scrolls past.
7 of 27 copy ads use claim words like clinically and cure, which limits reach. Swap them for what players noticed, like the stand mixer, in three new ads.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 30 Oct 2026
points: 7 of 27 copy ads use claim words like clinically and cure, which limits reach. Swap them for what players noticed, like the stand mixer, in three new ads.
None of the 30 ads shows a proof number, so buyers only get the promise. Collect one you can stand behind, like a review count or orders shipped, and open three new ads with it on the creative.

7 of 27 copy ads open on the same line, every single ticket unlocks a prize, and the rest are single use. That one pitch leads the copy, so buyers hear the same promise again. Test two new angles against it.
6 ads have run 60+ days, yet none of the 24 newer ads reuses a winner’s opening line. Build the next three ads as variations of the oldest winner, keeping its opener and changing the prize shown.

ads_1: Prize led creative built on what players noticed, with claim words cut
